transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My mind keeps getting stuck on these scary “what if I mess up the numbers and ruin something” thoughts, and I can’t turn them off. It’s just starting to feel really overwhelming, and I don't know how to make it stop.

When these thoughts come up, do you feel driven to do something over and over—like checking, counting, or repeating things—to relieve the anxiety? Also, did this start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

Yes, I find myself checking spreadsheet cells five or six times and logging into my bank app three or four times before bed until it finally feels "right." It really escalated after I moved into my own apartment and started my first full-time bookkeeping job, especially after I made a minor spreadsheet mistake at work that was quickly fixed.
Do you recognize that these repeated checking urges are excessive or unreasonable, even though you feel driven to do them? Or do they feel like a normal reaction to the recent move and job stress?

Yes, I definitely know it's excessive and doesn't make sense, especially since it takes up way too much of my time. But even though I realize that, I still get this intense, driving urge to keep checking until it finally feels "right." I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it, even when I want to.

Do these thoughts feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind against your will, or are they mainly worries that seem realistic and proportional to your actual responsibilities? Are they focused only on work and finances, or do they also show up in other areas?

They definitely feel intrusive and unwanted; even though I know these scary scenarios are highly unlikely, I just can't stop replaying and arguing with them in my head. Right now, they are strictly focused on my work with client spreadsheets and managing my own bills, rather than other areas of my life.

Besides the repeated checking, do you also have mental rituals like silently reviewing, counting, or repeating phrases to neutralize the thoughts? Or is the main problem the intrusive thoughts themselves?

I don't really do things like counting or repeating specific phrases, but I do find myself constantly trying to argue with the scary thoughts in my head to make them go away. Honestly, both the intrusive "what if" thoughts themselves and the physical checking are major parts of my struggle. They both just take up so much of my energy.

Between the intrusive “what if” thoughts and the repeated checking, which takes up more of your time and causes more distress for you? If you had to choose, is the main problem the thoughts themselves or the checking rituals?

It’s really hard to choose because both the thoughts and the checking work together to completely drain my daily well-being and productivity. They both cause so much misery and waste so much of my limited time that it feels like they're equally damaging to my life.
